subject: Mid-cycle uplift request: surge protection and co-term mechanics
messages:
From: Kelly Tran <kelly@opsora.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jul 2025 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-cycle capacity uplift and co-term options

Hi Soojin —

We’re seeing a higher-than-expected spike in inference usage for a new pilot (likely 3x baseline for a 6-week window). We want to secure short-term capacity so the app doesn’t degrade, but also don’t want to permanently commit at the higher level.

Questions:
- Can Redwood provide a temporary uplift that preserves part of our current discounted rate?
- Is there a way to co-term the uplift with our existing annual renewal (current term ends 2025-10-01)?
- Can we get an invoice split (50/50) if we sign an amendment mid-cycle?

Goal is minimal procurement hassle — legal is copied. If you can send a simple proposal or three options (fast/medium/secure), we’ll review with finance today.

Thanks,
Kelly Tran
Head of Ops, Opsora
kelly@opsora.com
Attachment: none

Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity uplift and co-term options

Hi Kelly —

Thanks for the context — appreciate the heads-up. High level, we can do two approaches that fit your constraints: a) a temporary staged top-up that buys surge capacity with a capped monthly minimum and a small uplift credit on renewal, or b) an instant permanent top-up with a short-term discount that you can choose to annualize at renewal.

I’ll outline both and include a short ‘safeguard’ variant (keeps a small reserve to maintain SLA if usage spikes beyond committed uplift). Can you confirm: peak tokens/month during the spike and whether you need the capacity immediately (this week) or can wait for a 48–72h provisioning window?

I’m looping Ben (pricing) and Monica (customer success / SLA) for pricing + operational readiness; Jordan for legal/contract pathing. I’ll follow up with a one-page proposal and a draft amendment you can share with procurement.

Best,
Soojín Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Mid-cycle capacity uplift and co-term options (pricing notes)

Soojín / team —

Notes from pricing side after quick calc:
- Baseline commit: Opsora current committed units = 1.2M token-units/month
- Expected pilot: peak ~3.6M token-units/month for 6 weeks

Proposed commercial structures (short list):
1) Staged Top-up (preferred) — 6-week uplift bucket of additional reserved units with a 10% uplift discount on those additional units for the duration. At renewal, remaining uplift (if converted to longer term) gets a 12% conversion credit applied against the first renewal invoice. No change to existing base price.

2) Surge-Safety Band — reserve 25% of peak as emergency capacity (hot standby) billed at a 7% premium but only activated if real-time usage crosses committed+uplift; lowers risk of throttling.

3) Instant Uplift (simple) — set new temporary commit at 3.6M/month for the remaining term, give a one-off one-month free credit (applied as invoice credit) and reduce additional units price by 5% for 3 months.

Billing / invoicing: we can split the amendment invoice into two invoices (50/50) as requested; finance needs PO or signed amendment before we break invoices.

Risks: supply-side — need to ensure model pool capacity for the 6-week window. Monica, can ops/infra confirm provisioning lead time? If >72h we should recommend staged top-up so capacity staged in advance.

Ben
VP, Pricing Ops

Kelly —

Attached is a concise proposal and an editable amendment draft for procurement (opsora-uplift-proposal-2025.pdf; opsora-sla-amendment-draft.docx). Summary below so you can share with finance/legal quickly:

Proposal summary (Staged Top-up + Safeguard) — 6-week window
- Temporary uplift: +2.4M token-units/month (adds to existing 1.2M) for a 6-week period starting on provisioning date.
- Price: additional units billed at your current committed rate minus 10% (temporary concession).
- Renewal conversion credit: if Opsora converts any or all of the uplift into the annual commit at renewal (term 2025-10-01), Redwood will apply a 12% conversion credit against the first renewal invoice for the converted portion.
- Surge safeguard: optional hot standby 25% of peak (600k units) billed as reserve at a 7% premium, only charged if activated. This keeps your production SLA intact if usage spikes beyond the uplift.
- Invoicing: Redwood can issue the amendment invoice split 50/50 on request.
- Timeline: provisioning lead-time 48–72 hours once amendment signed and PO received.
- Next steps: if agreeable, sign the attached amendment (DocuSign link below) and confirm preferred provisioning date; list procurement PO # and invoice split instruction.

Attachments: opsora-uplift-proposal-2025.pdf (PDF, 324KB) — one-page commercial summary; opsora-sla-amendment-draft.docx (DOCX, 78KB) — editable amendment + SLA addendum.
